rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is no performance baseline at all. The most critical unknown is whether any multimodal or complex configuration actually outperforms a simple unimodal model. Without a floor, we cannot judge whether added complexity (second modality, transformer aggregation, learned encoders) is justified. 2) What this tests: config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is a minimal, standard RNA-only baseline using the simplest encoder (PCA), simplest aggregation (avgpool), and the more informative multiprofile setting. It establishes the performance floor for the primary modality in cellular profiling. 3) Why it is the best first use of budget: Starting with the simplest viable model minimizes training failure risk, gives a clean reference signal, and immediately frames every subsequent multimodal experiment as a test of 'does adding the image modality / a learned encoder / a different fusion strategy improve over this baseline?' This single number will inform whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal exploration or in refining unimodal representations, making it the highest-information-density first experiment.

With only one completed experiment (config_006: rna_only, pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool → 59.1% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether adding the image modality provides any benefit over RNA alone. Config_004 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the minimal, direct extension of config_006: it keeps the RNA encoder (pca_n2000), profile setting (multiprofile), and aggregation (avgpool) identical, and only adds an image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with a standard weighted fusion. This isolates the effect of the image modality. If config_004 substantially outperforms config_006, it confirms image adds signal and justifies further investment in multimodal designs; if it performs similarly or worse, it redirects the search toward RNA-encoder or aggregation improvements. Under a limited budget, resolving this foundational question before exploring encoder variants, fusion strategies, or profile settings is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: config_004 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieved acc=0.6352, a clear +4.5pp improvement over the rna-only baseline config_006 (acc=0.5907) with all other settings identical, confirming that image modality contributes. Uncertainty: we do not yet know whether the 'weighted' fusion strategy is optimal or whether a simpler 'concat' fusion would perform comparably or better. Question: config_011 changes only the fusion from 'weighted' to 'concat' while holding model_setting, profile_setting, RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation constant relative to config_004. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy. Why best next: it is a clean single-variable A/B comparison against the current best result, directly informs a fundamental design decision (how to combine modal representations), and the outcome—whether fusion strategy matters or is relatively insensitive—will guide whether subsequent budget is better spent on aggregation, encoder choice, or profile setting.

Evidence: Our best config (config_004, acc=0.635) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted fusion, and we've confirmed multimodal > rna_only (~4.5% gain) and weighted > concat (~0.65% acc, ~1.9% F1 gain). However, we have only tested one image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and one RNA encoder (pca_n2000), leaving major uncertainty about whether the specific image backbone is a critical design choice. Question: config_036 is a clean single-variable swap of the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while holding all other settings identical to config_004 (pca_n2000, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile). This isolates the effect of image encoder architecture. Why best next: Under a tight budget, establishing whether the image encoder is a bottleneck (or not) is foundational—if resnet50 performs comparably, we know the image side is not the limiting factor and should pivot to RNA encoder or aggregation; if imagenet_vit_l is clearly superior, we confirm our choice and can confidently explore other dimensions. This is more informative than jumping to a multi-variable change (e.g., new RNA encoder + new aggregation) and directly extends our strongest evidence.

Evidence: All four completed experiments use avgpool aggregation, so the effect of aggregation is entirely unexplored. The current best (config_036: pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.639) gives a strong baseline. config_013 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding the best-performing RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), fusion (weighted), and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. This isolates the aggregation effect cleanly. Question tested: Does transformer-based aggregation of multiprofile representations improve over simple average pooling? Why this is the best next experiment: Aggregation is a fundamental architectural choice that has zero coverage in the experiment history, and it is a high-leverage design decision—if transformer aggregation helps, it opens a new optimization axis; if it does not, we confirm avgpool sufficiency and can redirect budget toward RNA encoder or profile-setting variations. It is a single-variable change from the current best, maximizing information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The current best config (config_036: pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.639) shows that adding image modality to RNA helps (~5 pts over RNA-only), weighted fusion beats concat, avgpool beats transformer aggregation, and resnet50 marginally edges ViT-L. However, all experiments so far use pca_n2000 for RNA—a simple linear projection. The RNA encoder is the largest untested design axis. Question: Does a learned nonlinear RNA representation (scvi_n200) improve upon PCA when all other components are held at their empirically best settings? config_038 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 relative to config_036, cleanly isolating the representation effect. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a single-variable comparison against our strongest baseline, directly tests whether the RNA bottleneck is representation quality (linear vs. learned), and the answer will determine whether to invest remaining budget in more complex RNA encoders (scgpt) or instead explore the profile-setting axis. If scvi_n200 matches or beats PCA, it validates learned representations and motivates testing scgpt; if it underperforms, PCA suffices and we should pivot to profile setting or image-encoder refinements.

Evidence: The largest performance jump so far came from switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (config_036: 0.6390 → config_038: 0.6776, with resnet50/avgpool/weighted). Meanwhile, pca_n2000 shows near-parity between imagenet_vit_l (0.6352) and resnet50 (0.6390). Question: Does the scvi_n200 improvement generalize to imagenet_vit_l, or is it specific to the resnet50 pairing? Testing config_001 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) completes a clean 2×2 factorial over {pca_n2000, scvi_n200} × {resnet50, imagenet_vit_l} with all other factors held constant, isolating the RNA-encoder and image-encoder main effects and their interaction. Why best next: It is a single-variable change from the current best (config_038), directly extends the strongest evidence, and the resulting 2×2 will clarify whether to invest further in scvi_n200 broadly or only in specific pairings—critical information before spending budget on aggregation/fusion variants.

Evidence: config_001 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7062 acc. The only design choice with weak/ambiguous evidence is fusion: with pca_n2000, weighted (0.6352) beat concat (0.6287) by a narrow 0.65% margin (config_004 vs config_011). This small gap suggests the optimal fusion strategy may depend on the quality of the underlying representations. Question: Does concat fusion outperform or match weighted fusion when paired with the stronger scvi_n200 RNA encoder? config_042 changes only fusion (weighted→concat) from the best config, isolating this single variable. Why this is the best next experiment: It is the lowest-risk, highest-information exploitation step—either it improves on the current best (giving a new top config) or it confirms weighted fusion is robustly superior across encoder choices, closing out the fusion design question so future experiments can focus on other axes (e.g., scgpt, singleprofile, or image-only baselines).

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder (0.7062–0.7150 in multimodal vs. 0.6352–0.6390 for pca_n2000), and the current best config (042) pairs scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and concat. However, we have no data on how well scvi_n200 performs as a standalone RNA-only model. config_006 shows pca_n2000 rna_only at 0.5907, but the jump from pca to scvi in the multimodal setting was ~4–7%, so the RNA-only ceiling with scvi is unknown. Question: config_048 (scvi_n200, rna_only, multiprofile, avgpool) is a clean single-variable ablation against config_001 (same RNA encoder, aggregation, profile; only the image modality is removed). It directly quantifies the marginal contribution of the image modality when the RNA representation is strong. Why best next experiment: If scvi_n200 rna_only approaches ~0.68–0.70, the image adds little and further multimodal tuning has diminishing returns, redirecting budget toward RNA encoder improvements (e.g., scgpt) or profile settings. If it drops to ~0.60–0.63, the image modality is essential and we should continue exploiting the multimodal direction. Either way, this single experiment resolves a major architectural uncertainty that would otherwise cloud every subsequent comparison, making it the highest-information-per-experiment choice under the limited budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 consistently outperforms pca_n2000 across all tested settings (+0.04 to +0.07 acc), and the best configuration so far is config_042 (scvi_n200 + vit_l + avgpool + concat, 0.715 acc). However, scgpt has never been tested, leaving a major uncertainty about the RNA encoder landscape. Question: config_040 (scgpt + vit_l + avgpool + concat) is a clean A/B comparison against config_042, isolating the RNA encoder effect while holding image encoder, aggregation, and fusion at their best-known values. Why best next experiment: it tests the single most important unexplored design dimension (RNA encoder type) under the strongest known configuration. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new promising direction; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as the optimal RNA representation and redirects budget toward other axes (e.g., singleprofile, transformer aggregation). This is more informative than re-testing transformer aggregation (already shown to hurt in config_013 vs config_036) or image_only baselines (multimodal advantage is already well-established at +0.056 to +0.065 over rna_only).
